title: Localized quotient setup
statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, Λ a Noetherian geometrically regular k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], q a prime ideal, and n ≥ 1. Set L = Λ_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], J = qL, and B = L/J^n. Then B is Artinian and local with maximal ideal the image of J, and H1Cotangent k (ResidueField B) is finite over ResidueField B [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 07FH, first paragraph of proof; Tag 07E5

proof.text: Localize Λ at q. L is Noetherian local with maximal ideal J. Purely inseparable base change commutes with localization, so localization of regular rings gives geometric regularity of L.

The characteristic p of a field is prime since p > 0. Apply the geometric-regularity injectivity theorem to L. Its residue cotangent homology injects into J/J², which is finite dimensional because J is finitely generated.

Since n ≥ 1, J^n is proper with radical J. The quotient B is Noetherian local of dimension zero, hence Artinian, with maximal ideal the image of J. The third isomorphism theorem identifies its residue field as a k-algebra with the residue field of L. H1Cotangent functoriality for this isomorphism and its inverse transports finiteness.

    ∃ hArt : IsArtinianRing (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
